pr_title: Don't try to add special tokens to the matcher in XGrammar.
pr_body:
Prevent XGrammar from attempting to match on special tokens. XGrammar throws the assertion on the C++ side if we send it a special token for acceptance, which crashes the whole engine. This fix uses XGrammar's `tokenizer_info` to skip over these tokens before we submit them and get crashed.

FIX #11044 ; see that issue for the original traceback.

There may be a better way to do this than just continuing over the last token while it's special, but this is sufficient to resolve the crash for me and I'm noticing no slowdown or additional issues in outputs. Thanks!

Hi @sjuxax, thanks for your contribution to vLLM! 

I think these special tokens should be forbidden from generated by xgrammar. As I discussed in this [previous comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11044#issuecomment-2548356421), I am wondering if you could provide the specific code that caused the error, or the model, prompt, and output structure. I believe by investigating the reasons behind these token generations, we can further resolve the issue.
From #14868 xgrammar now can handle special tokens accordingly based on the encoded vocab, which should resolve this issue.

comments:
Hi @sjuxax, thanks for the bug report! 

XGrammar should mask out the special tokens and avoid them being generated. So it would be helpful if we could further investigate why the unk token is generated. Could you provide a reproducible script so I can further dig into that?
@sfc-gh-zhwang Which version of xgrammar are you using? I think latest version of xgrammar should be able to support special tokens.

review_comments: Hi there, I don't think this assert is necessary.
move to under L250 and use sampled_token to avoid additional access here.
